description: Study of vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and their applications. Covers systems of linear equations, determinants, eigenvalues, orthogonality, and diagonalization.

modules.title: Systems of Linear Equations and Matrices

concepts.title: Systems of Linear Equations and Augmented Matrices
learning_objectives: Represent a system of linear equations as an augmented matrix
Perform elementary row operations on an augmented matrix
Classify systems as consistent (unique or infinite solutions) or inconsistent

concepts.title: Row Echelon Form and Gaussian Elimination
learning_objectives: Reduce an augmented matrix to row echelon form (REF) using Gaussian elimination
Reduce to reduced row echelon form (RREF) using Gauss-Jordan elimination
Identify pivot positions, free variables, and express solutions parametrically

concepts.title: Matrix Operations
learning_objectives: Perform matrix addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication
Compute the transpose of a matrix and identify symmetric matrices
Verify that matrix multiplication is associative but not commutative

concepts.title: Matrix Inverses
learning_objectives: Determine whether a square matrix is invertible
Compute the inverse of a matrix using row reduction of [A | I]
Solve linear systems Ax = b by computing x = A⁻¹b when A is invertible

concepts.title: Determinants and Their Properties
learning_objectives: Compute determinants of 2×2 and 3×3 matrices using cofactor expansion
Apply properties of determinants (row operations, transpose, product rule)
Use the determinant to test invertibility of a matrix

concepts.title: Cramer's Rule and the Adjugate
learning_objectives: Apply Cramer's Rule to solve n×n systems with a unique solution
Compute the adjugate (classical adjoint) of a matrix
Express the inverse of a matrix as A⁻¹ = (1/det A) adj A

concepts.title: Geometric Interpretation of the Determinant
learning_objectives: Interpret the absolute value of the determinant as the scaling factor for area (2D) or volume (3D)
Relate the sign of the determinant to orientation preservation or reversal
Use determinants to compute the area of a parallelogram and the volume of a parallelepiped

concepts.title: Vector Spaces and Subspaces
learning_objectives: State the axioms of a vector space
Verify whether a given set with operations is a vector space
Determine whether a subset of a vector space is a subspace

concepts.title: Linear Independence, Span, and Basis
learning_objectives: Determine whether a set of vectors is linearly independent
Determine whether a vector is in the span of a given set
Find a basis for a vector space or subspace

concepts.title: Dimension and the Rank-Nullity Theorem
learning_objectives: Determine the dimension of a vector space from a basis
Compute the rank (dimension of column space) and nullity (dimension of null space) of a matrix
Apply the Rank-Nullity Theorem: rank(A) + nullity(A) = n

concepts.title: Column Space, Null Space, and Row Space
learning_objectives: Find bases for the column space, null space, and row space of a matrix
Interpret the null space as the solution set of Ax = 0
Relate the column space to the range of possible outputs b in Ax = b

concepts.title: Linear Transformations and Their Properties
learning_objectives: Define a linear transformation and verify linearity from the definition
Determine the image and kernel of a linear transformation
Compose linear transformations and relate composition to matrix multiplication

concepts.title: Matrix Representation of Linear Transformations
learning_objectives: Find the standard matrix of a linear transformation from Rⁿ to Rᵐ
Compute the matrix of a linear transformation with respect to given bases
Apply change-of-basis matrices to convert between representations

concepts.title: Geometric Transformations in R² and R³
learning_objectives: Identify rotation, reflection, projection, and shear as linear transformations
Write the standard matrices for common geometric transformations
Compose geometric transformations and interpret the resulting matrix

concepts.title: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
learning_objectives: Find eigenvalues by solving the characteristic equation det(A − λI) = 0
Find eigenvectors corresponding to each eigenvalue by solving (A − λI)x = 0
Determine algebraic and geometric multiplicities of eigenvalues

concepts.title: Diagonalization
learning_objectives: Determine whether a matrix is diagonalizable
Diagonalize a matrix A = PDP⁻¹ where D is diagonal
Use diagonalization to compute powers of a matrix Aⁿ

concepts.title: Complex Eigenvalues
learning_objectives: Find complex eigenvalues and eigenvectors of real matrices
Write real-valued general solutions from complex eigenvalue pairs
Interpret complex eigenvalues geometrically as rotation-scaling

concepts.title: Applications of Eigenvalues
learning_objectives: Model discrete dynamical systems xₖ₊₁ = Axₖ and analyze long-term behavior
Apply eigenvalue analysis to Markov chains and find steady-state vectors
Use the Cayley-Hamilton theorem to express matrix polynomials

concepts.title: Inner Products and Orthogonality
learning_objectives: Define the standard inner product (dot product) in Rⁿ and general inner product spaces
Determine orthogonality and compute orthogonal complements
Decompose a vector into components parallel and perpendicular to a subspace

concepts.title: The Gram-Schmidt Process
learning_objectives: Apply the Gram-Schmidt process to produce an orthonormal basis from a given basis
Compute the QR factorization of a matrix using Gram-Schmidt
Solve least squares problems using QR factorization

concepts.title: Orthogonal Projections and Least Squares
learning_objectives: Compute the orthogonal projection of a vector onto a subspace
Set up and solve least squares problems Ax ≈ b using the normal equations AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb
Apply least squares to fit a line or polynomial to data

concepts.title: Symmetric Matrices and the Spectral Theorem
learning_objectives: Prove that eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix are real
Prove that eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix are orthogonal
Orthogonally diagonalize a symmetric matrix A = QDQᵀ

concepts.title: Quadratic Forms and Definiteness
learning_objectives: Express a quadratic form Q(x) = xᵀAx and identify its associated symmetric matrix
Classify a quadratic form as positive definite, negative definite, or indefinite using eigenvalues
Apply Sylvester's criterion (leading principal minors) to test definiteness

concepts.title: The Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
learning_objectives: Compute the singular values and singular vectors of a matrix
Construct the full SVD factorization A = UΣVᵀ
Interpret the SVD geometrically as a rotation-scaling-rotation decomposition

concepts.title: Applications of the SVD
learning_objectives: Apply the SVD to compute the pseudoinverse and solve least squares problems
Use low-rank SVD approximation for data compression (image compression, dimensionality reduction)
Compute the condition number of a matrix and assess numerical stability

modules.title: Abstract Vector Spaces and Function Spaces

concepts.title: General Vector Spaces (Polynomials, Matrices, Functions)
learning_objectives: Verify that the space of polynomials of degree ≤ n is a vector space
Verify that the space of m×n matrices is a vector space
Find bases and dimensions for polynomial and matrix spaces

concepts.title: Inner Product Spaces and Fourier Series Preview
learning_objectives: Define inner products on function spaces (e.g., ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫ f(x)g(x) dx)
Verify orthogonality of trigonometric functions {sin(nx), cos(nx)} on [−π, π]
Compute Fourier coefficients as projections onto an orthogonal basis

concepts.title: LU Decomposition
learning_objectives: Factor a matrix A = LU using Gaussian elimination without row swaps
Apply partial pivoting to obtain PA = LU when row swaps are needed
Solve systems efficiently using forward and back substitution with LU decomposition

concepts.title: Iterative Methods for Linear Systems
learning_objectives: Apply Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterations to solve large linear systems
Determine convergence conditions for iterative methods
Compare direct and iterative methods in terms of efficiency and applicability

concepts.title: Eigenvalue Algorithms
learning_objectives: Apply the power method to find the dominant eigenvalue and eigenvector
Apply the inverse power method with shifts to find specific eigenvalues
Describe the QR algorithm for computing all eigenvalues of a matrix

projects.title: Image Compression with the SVD
projects.description: Represent a grayscale image as a matrix, compute its SVD, and reconstruct the image using rank-k approximations for various values of k. Analyze the trade-off between compression ratio and image quality.
learning_objectives: Compute the SVD of a large matrix and extract singular values
Reconstruct low-rank approximations and measure information retained
Quantify the compression ratio and quality trade-off

projects.title: Google PageRank as a Markov Chain
projects.description: Model a small web graph as a Markov chain, construct the Google matrix, and compute the PageRank vector using eigenvalue methods (power iteration) and direct computation.
learning_objectives: Construct a stochastic matrix from a directed graph
Apply the power method to find the dominant eigenvector
Interpret the steady-state vector as page importance rankings

projects.title: Polynomial Curve Fitting with Least Squares
projects.description: Given a set of noisy data points, fit polynomials of varying degree using the least squares method. Analyze residuals and discuss overfitting vs. underfitting.
learning_objectives: Set up the Vandermonde matrix for polynomial fitting
Solve the normal equations to find the least squares polynomial
Evaluate model quality using residual analysis
